mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW Z4 22i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full BMW Z4 22i engine replacement typically costs £1,800-£2,600 supply-only for a rebuilt M54B22 unit, or £2,200-£3,800 fitted by a specialist. Used M54B22 engines: £800-£1,600 depending on mileage and condition. Reconditioned units: £1,400-£2,200. Professional fitting adds £800-£1,500 to the engine cost.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW Z4 22i M54B22 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M54B22 is generally a robust and characterful straight-six engine. However, with the youngest examples now over 20 years old, age-related issues are common. The most frequent problems are oil leaks (valve cover gasket and oil filter housing), CCV system failure causing oil consumption, VANOS seal degradation, and cooling system component failure. Regular maintenance and proactive replacement of known weak points are essential for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of VANOS failure in a BMW Z4 22i M54B22?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs of VANOS failure in the Z4 22i are: hesitation or flat spot on acceleration, particularly below 3,000rpm; loss of low-end torque and poor throttle response; rattling noise from the front of the engine at idle; reduced fuel economy.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a BMW Z4 22i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Z4 22i worth £3,000-£8,000, a £2,200-£3,800 rebuilt engine can make financial sense if the body, gearbox, and interior are in good condition - particularly given the E85 Z4's rising classic status. Compare replacement cost against vehicle value - replacement is viable up to approximately 70% of the car's value. Well-maintained examples with good bodywork are worth saving. Always factor the 12-month warranty into your replacement decision.

mainEntity.name: What causes the BMW Z4 22i M54B22 CCV system to fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CCV (crankcase ventilation) system's oil separator diaphragm fails due to age and heat cycling, allowing oil to be drawn into the intake manifold. Symptoms include oil consumption, blue smoke from exhaust, rough idle, and misfires. Replacement with an updated cold-weather version is recommended. Cost at a specialist is £300-£550.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my BMW Z4 22i engine with a different engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Engine swaps to a different size or type are technically complex and rarely cost-effective for the Z4 22i. The M54B22 is the only engine fitted to the 22i from the factory - stick to like-for-like replacement. Swapping to a 2.5i or 3.0i (M54B25/M54B30) requires different ECU, wiring, and potentially transmission. Swapping to an N52 (facelift engine) requires significant modification. Insurance must be notified of any non-standard engine swap. Our marketplace only recommends like-for-like code-matching for warranty coverage.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW Z4 22i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW Z4 22i arrived in October 2003 as the entry-level straight-six variant of the E85 Z4 range, powered by the M54B22 2.2-litre naturally aspirated engine. Slotting between the 2.0i four-cylinder and the 2.5i/3.0i six-cylinder models, the 22i offered the smooth, refined character of BMW's inline-six at a more accessible price point. Production ran until October 2005, when the facelift E85 models transitioned to the N52 engine family.

milestones.description: October 2003 - BMW Z4 22i (E85) launches with the M54B22 2.2-litre naturally aspirated straight-six petrol engine, producing 170hp and 210Nm of torque
2005 - Z4 22i production continues with the M54B22 engine unchanged; available with 5-speed manual or 5-speed automatic transmission
October 2005 - Z4 22i discontinued as E85 facelift introduces N52 engine family; the 2.2-litre displacement is not carried over

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW Z4 22i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW Z4 22i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW Z4 22i is powered exclusively by the M54B22 2.2-litre straight-six - a smooth, characterful engine that shares its architecture with the larger M54B30. However, with production ending in 2005, all examples are now 20+ years old, and age-related failures are common. Every rebuilt M54B22 engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: CCV System Failure - Why the BMW Z4 22i M54B22 Burns Oil and Runs Rough
problems.rootCause: The crankcase ventilation valve (CCV) system's oil separator diaphragm fails, allowing oil to be drawn into the intake manifold. This causes oil consumption, blue smoke from the exhaust, rough idle, and eventually catalytic converter damage if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace CCV valve, hoses, and oil separator with updated cold-weather version
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000-100,000 miles. Prevents oil consumption and misfires

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace CCV system and intake manifold gaskets while manifold is removed
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if manifold is off for CCV access

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - rebuilt/reconditioned engine (catastrophic oil starvation)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M54B22 with upgraded CCV components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation caused bearing damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW Z4 22i in the UK is worth between £3,000 and £8,000 depending on condition and mileage. With a full rebuilt engine costing £2,200-£3,800 fitted, replacement cost can approach a significant portion of the vehicle's value. However, for well-maintained examples with good bodies and interiors, replacement is often worthwhile - particularly given the rising classic status of the E85 Z4.
problems.recommendation: If your Z4 22i shows signs of oil consumption or rough idle, have the CCV system inspected immediately. A £300-£550 specialist replacement is far cheaper than a £2,200-£3,800 engine rebuild. If the engine has already suffered oil starvation and bearing damage, only a full rebuilt engine will save the car.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M54B22 BMW Z4 22i engine prices

problems.h4: VANOS Seal Failure - Why the BMW Z4 22i M54B22 Loses Low-End Power
problems.rootCause: The double-VANOS system uses rubber seals that harden and shrink over time. This allows oil pressure to bleed off, reducing the system's ability to advance or retard cam timing. Symptoms include hesitation on acceleration, loss of low-end torque, poor fuel economy, and a rattling noise from the front of the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace VANOS seals with upgraded Teflon seals

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - VANOS rebuild + timing chain guides
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace seals, timing chain guides, and tensioner while VANOS is removed
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if timing chain rattle is also present

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - rebuilt/reconditioned engine (catastrophic timing failure)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M54B22 with upgraded VANOS and timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if timing chain has jumped or snapped

problems.recommendation: VANOS seal failure is one of the most common M54 issues, but it's also one of the cheapest to fix. A £350-£650 specialist seal replacement using upgraded Teflon seals restores full performance and is significantly cheaper than engine replacement. If your Z4 22i feels flat below 3,000rpm, have the VANOS system inspected before considering more expensive repairs.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M54B22 BMW Z4 22i engine prices

problems.h4: Cooling System Failure - Why the BMW Z4 22i M54B22 Overheats
problems.rootCause: The M54's cooling system uses plastic components - water pump impeller, thermostat housing, and expansion tank - that become brittle with age. Failure leads to coolant loss, overheating, and potentially a warped cylinder head or cracked block.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat, expansion tank, hoses, coolant flush
Replace head gasket, skim head, pressure test for cracks
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if block and bottom end are undamaged

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - rebuilt/reconditioned engine (cracked head / block)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M54B22 with new cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if head is cracked or block damaged

problems.recommendation: On a 20+ year-old Z4 22i, preventative cooling system overhaul is essential. For under £750 at a specialist, you can replace all critical cooling components and avoid the risk of overheating. If your Z4 has already overheated and the head gasket has failed, a specialist head gasket replacement (£800-£1,400) is viable if the head isn't cracked. If the head is cracked, only a full rebuilt engine will save the car.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M54B22 BMW Z4 22i engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Leaks - Why the BMW Z4 22i M54B22 Leaves Oil Spots
problems.rootCause: The valve cover gasket and oil filter housing gasket harden and shrink over time, allowing oil to seep out. Oil drips onto the exhaust manifold, creating a burning smell, and can eventually lead to low oil levels and engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket, clean oil residue
repairOptions.longevity: Quick, cost-effective fix for visible oil leaks

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - oil filter housing gasket replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil filter housing gasket, oil change
Supply & fit rebuilt M54B22 with new gaskets, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil loss caused bearing or camshaft damage

problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the M54B22 are rarely catastrophic if caught early. The valve cover gasket is the most common and cheapest to fix - address it as soon as you notice the burning oil smell or oil spots. The oil filter housing gasket is next most common and should be replaced promptly to prevent oil dripping onto the serpentine belt. On a Z4 22i, regular oil level checks are essential - don't rely solely on the electronic sensor.
